requirements_summary: Primary workload: real-time reranking + short-turn chat for ops staff. Must support sustained throughput for peak load windows (US freight batch windows). Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for prompts <= 64 tokens; p99 < 1s for typical routes. Cost sensitivity moderate—willing to commit reserved GPUs for predictable pricing if throughput guarantees accepted. Deployment: VPC-first with eventual on-prem appliance; strict residency for EU operations. Must support SSO (SAML), KMS-integrated keys, and audit logs for all inference calls.
negotiation_points: Customer requests a sustained min throughput guarantee: 12k tokens/sec across reserved pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT).
Concurrency caps: propose soft cap at 48 concurrent connections with graceful queuing; customer requests hard caps per-tenant (24) to protect multi-tenant pipelines.
Burst policy: customer wants bursts up to 3x sustained (36k tokens/sec) for up to 90s; Redwood proposes 2x for 60s with prioritized preemption rules.
GPUs reserved: initial ask 10x A100-80GB equivalent dedicated; ops countered with baseline 8 + burst pool of 2 reserved for autoscale/spot-bursting.

SLA credit model: customer prefers credits tied to failure of min tokens/sec for continuous 10-minute windows; Redwood proposes sliding-window measurement and credits for sustained 30-minute shortfall.
Fallback behavior: explicit model routing policy required for graceful degradation (route to smaller quantized variant with proportional latency/cost tradeoff).
